array_traversal.quote: i goes from 0 to a.length; Using <= or < makes no difference here; because both go through the whole array; so it visits each element once
array_traversal.rule: wrong rule: < vs <= and 0..n vs 0..n-1 are interchangeable. Right rule: for (i = 0; i < n; i++) runs n times with i going up to n - 1; with <= it runs n + 1 times and reaches i = n.

for_loop.quote: Using <= or < makes no difference here; because both go through the whole array; so it visits each element once
for_loop.rule: wrong rule: An array loop processes the whole array from index 0 to length-1 and increments its index at the end of the body, whatever the code says. Right rule: The loop visits exactly the indices that its initialisation, guard and update produce, in the order in which its statements are written.

off_by_one_error.quote: i goes from 0 to a.length; Using <= or < makes no difference here; because both go through the whole array; so it visits each element once
off_by_one_error.rule: wrong rule: < and <= (and 0..n versus 0..n-1) are interchangeable in a loop bound. Right rule: i < N runs N times from 0 and i <= N runs N+1 times; with an array of length N only i < N stays inside the indices 0..N-1.
